sights.w: Encyclopedic collection of 67,000+ works spanning 6,000 years, perched in Eden Park; general admission and parking are always free.
sights.k: Free general admission; closed Mondays (Tue–Sun 11–5, Thu to 8).

sights.w: European old masters (Rembrandt, Turner, Hals, Ingres) plus Chinese porcelains and French Renaissance enamels inside an 1820 Federal mansion with Robert S. Duncanson murals; bequeathed to the city in 1927.
sights.k: Historic house museum, small but exceptional; check hours.

sights.w: Zaha Hadid's 2003 Lois & Richard Rosenthal Center — the first American art museum designed by a woman, an internationally studied piece of architecture at 6th & Walnut.
sights.k: Rotating contemporary shows; the building itself is the draw.

sights.w: The nation's largest public sign museum — a glowing indoor streetscape of vintage neon and Americana signage in Camp Washington.
sights.k: Closed Mon–Tue (Wed–Sun 10–4).

sights.w: 200+ years of firefighting history in the restored 1906 Court Street Firehouse — Cincinnati created the nation's first paid professional fire department in 1853.
sights.k: Housed in a National Register 1906 firehouse; limited hours.

sights.w: Ohio's oldest brick house (1804) and the anchor of the Betts-Longworth Historic District — now a small museum of the built environment in the West End.
sights.k: Very small; check for open days/guided tours.

sights.w: Northern Kentucky's regional history and natural history museum, set inside Devou Park with skyline views over the river.
sights.k: In Devou Park (NKY); closed Mondays.

sights.w: Cincinnati's grand hilltop park above the river — the Twin Lakes overlook gives one of the best Ohio River views in the city, plus the Presidential Grove of memorial oaks (first planted 1882 for Washington).
sights.k: Free, open daily; overlook is in the NE corner.

sights.w: Art Deco glasshouse in Eden Park (1933) with rainforest, desert and orchid houses and a beloved annual spring butterfly show.
sights.k: Small admission for special shows; closed Mondays.

sights.w: 224-acre Mt. Lookout park crowned by a 1930 Italian Renaissance pavilion; climb to the overlook for panoramic views across the Little Miami valley.
sights.k: Free; hilltop pavilion is a popular event venue.

sights.w: At 1,459 acres Cincinnati's largest park and one of the country's largest urban forests, with miles of trails and a free 120-acre arboretum.
sights.k: Free; huge — pick a trailhead or the arboretum.

sights.w: A National Historic Landmark garden cemetery (1844) — 733 acres of lakes, monuments and champion trees, one of the largest cemeteries in the US and a designated arboretum.
sights.k: Free; a working cemetery — be respectful.

sights.w: 1,000+ acres of woodland trails, ponds and a nature center in Milford — a longtime regional favorite for hiking and birding.
sights.k: Admission/membership; east-suburb drive.

sights.w: Hilltop Mt. Lookout park on Mt. Tusculum with several overlooks taking in the Ohio and Little Miami rivers, the NKY hills and Lunken Airport.
sights.k: Free, open daily 6a–10p.

sights.w: The oldest professional observatory in the US and 'Birthplace of American Astronomy,' with one of the world's oldest working telescopes; on its Mt. Lookout hilltop since 1873.
sights.k: Public viewing nights and tours — check schedule.

sights.w: Hillside artists' neighborhood of steep streets and skyline views; its 1859 Immaculata Church draws 10,000+ pilgrims each Good Friday to 'Pray the Steps' up St. Gregory St.
sights.k: Church is active; the Good Friday steps tradition is the signature draw.

sights.w: Clifton Heights hillside park with a grand, wide-open view over the entire Cincinnati basin, downtown skyline and the Ohio River.
sights.k: Free; small neighborhood park (not the NKY Bellevue).

sights.w: One of the best-preserved Moorish Revival buildings in the US (1866), a National Historic Landmark tied to Reform Judaism founder Rabbi Isaac Mayer Wise.
sights.k: Active synagogue; interior by tour/arrangement.

sights.n: Cathedral Basilica of St. Peter in Chains
sights.w: Greek Revival 'White Angel' cathedral (1845) at 8th & Plum with a soaring spire and mosaic interior, seat of the Archdiocese of Cincinnati.
sights.k: Active cathedral; open for visits around services.

sights.n: William Howard Taft National Historic Site
sights.w: NPS-run birthplace and boyhood home of the only man to serve as both US President and Chief Justice, in the Mt. Auburn Historic District.
sights.k: Free NPS site; ranger tours of the restored home.

sights.w: Walnut Hills home where the future 'Uncle Tom's Cabin' author lived; now an Ohio History Connection museum on abolition and Cincinnati's Black history, reopened after a $2.5M renovation.
sights.k: Limited hours; recently renovated.

sights.w: A medieval-style stone castle on the Little Miami River hand-built over decades starting 1927 by WWI vet and Boy Scout leader Harry Andrews — a beloved regional oddity.
sights.k: Seasonal/weekend hours; NE-suburb drive to Loveland.

sights.w: The 1892 Tudor-style Mt. Adams pottery works of famed Rookwood Pottery, its old kilns big enough to dine in; now a restaurant/bar with skyline views.
sights.k: Building now a restaurant — exterior/architecture and kiln dining rooms are the draw.

sights.w: Cincinnati's most charming shopping square, centered on the classical 1900 Kilgour Fountain and a grassy green, lined with 100+ boutiques and cafes.
sights.k: Walkable district; Sunday farmers' market mid-May–Oct.

sights.w: A National Historic Landmark 'garden city' — one of America's first fully planned suburbs, laid out in the 1920s by Mary Emery and John Nolen in Tudor-village style with a central concourse and carillon.
sights.k: Historic village ~10 mi east; stroll the square.

sights.address: Hamilton Ave & Hoffner St, Cincinnati, OH 45223
sights.w: Cincinnati's most eclectic, creative neighborhood — a two-mile stretch of Hamilton Ave lined with locally-owned restaurants, vintage shops, record stores and music venues amid the Italianate Hoffner Historic District.
sights.k: Best explored on foot; nightlife-heavy.

sights.w: Regional icon 24 miles NE in Mason — a 364-acre amusement park with 15+ coasters, an Eiffel Tower replica and the Soak City water park, open since 1972.
sights.k: Seasonal (spring–fall + Halloween/holiday events); paid admission.

sights.w: Once home to the world's largest indoor model-train display (25,000 sq ft, 2+ miles of track) in West Chester.
sights.k: CLOSED — permanently shut January 5, 2025. Listed for reference; do not visit.
